FORCE OF WILL - UNOFFICIAL DRAFT RULES V.01 - LOUSYSHRINEGOD
Pre-Draft, Each Player selects up to three J/Rulers that they own, and places them in front of them.
J/Rulers that a player has selected is public knowledge, and at any time a player may ask another player what their J/Ruler is.

Each player takes 4 packs of Force of Will, and places them in front of them. Players may not exchange, swap, or switch their packs once they have been selected and the draft has begun. Players may leave at any time during the draft, and take with them any unopened packs that they have, any cards they have drafted, and the pack they are currently drafting from, IF and only IF they have just opened that pack, the pack was originally one of their four packs, and no other player has selected a card from the pack. In the event that the pack that would currently be drafting does not meet any of those conditions they may not take their currently drafted pack with them when they leave. They still take any already drafted cards, and any unopened packs.

Leaving is acceptable, but not very sporting. Participating in a draft is a privilege, not a right, and players are not inherently obligated to accept unsporting behavior. However, players may leave at any point in time once the draft has started, and are under no obligation to continue, and cannot be forced to unopened packs they have for the draft, or cards already drafted.

It’s still a unsporting thing to do.

During the draft, players select one card from the booster pack, and then pass the pack to their left or right, alternating each round of the draft. When a player is passed a pack, the player selects one card from the pack, and then pass’s it to the appropriate player.

DRAFTING J/RULERS
When a J/Ruler is drafted, the drafting player must declare that they are selecting a J/Ruler, and place it among the J/Rulers that they have selected. This is due to the double sided nature of the cards, and to the fact that it would be difficult to disguise in the first place.

Players do not do anything special for all other cards.

DECK CONSTRUCTION Players may use any number of Basic Stones, as long as it would not break rules for normal deck construction. Players may only use as their J/Ruler one of the three J/Rulers that they selected at the start of the draft, or any J/Ruler that they drafted and announced prior to the end of the draft, and the start of the deck construction stage.

Players do not have to announce which J/Ruler they are using until the start of the Game Phase. J/Rulers held or available to each player is still public knowledge.

Players create a deck of at least 30 cards, and up to 40 cards. Players may only put cards in their deck that they selected during the draft. Players may not use any card that they did not pick during the draft. The players sideboard is considered to be any card that they picked during the draft, but do not have in their deck. Use of any card in the players deck that was not selected from a booster pack by that player during the draft is considered cheating, and will be subject to penalties. (Detailed below)

EXCEPTION: If a player is given a Promotional Card that is considered in terms of gameplay to be EXACTLY identical to a card that the player selected during the draft, they may, at the Judges discretion, substitute the Promotional Card for the drafted card in terms of deck construction. If the judge allows one player to do so, however, they must allow any other player in the draft to do so as well.

Example: Bob is given a Promotional Copy of Oz’s Magic for participating in the draft, or being at the event. The card is identical to a normal Oz’s Magic in terms of gameplay, size, card backing, and other factors, but perhaps features alternate art or foiling. Bob drafts 3 copies of Oz’s Magic. Bob may ask the Judge if he can remove one of his drafted copies of Oz’s Magic and replace it with the promotional card. If the judge says yes, Bob may replace one copy of Oz’s Magic with his promotional copy. Bob can no longer use the replaced copy in building his deck, nor is it considered to be a drafted card in terms of his sideboard. If the Judge says yes to Bob however, they must also allow Eve to use the promotional copy. Players must still notify the judge that they are doing so.

(Yikes, that was wayyyyy too long and wordy. )

Once all players have their decks, or a time limit has been reached, players select a J/Ruler. Players select their J/Ruler by writing on a piece of paper the J/Ruler that they intend to use for their deck. Players then all reveal their J/Rulers simultaneously. Players must write down the name of one of their selected J/Rulers, or a J/Ruler they drafted and declared. Format is decided before the draft starts, and cannot be changed irregardless of facts that might otherwise make it awkward, such as a player dropping out.

Suggested Formats include ladder, Round Robin, or a Swiss System matchup.
